description: Dillahunty argues that Christianity’s allegedly communicative God has not delivered verifiable support or a justifying explanation, so Christianity has not discharged its rational burden.
critique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty turns God’s claimed communicative capacity into an evidential expectation and connects its alleged nonfulfillment directly to rational withholding, yielding unusually strong responsiveness and motion-level burden relevance. Principal limitation: Although the excerpt says Christian claims lack “evidence or verifiable observation,” it neither examines the proffered evidence nor defends why divine communication should produce Dillahunty’s particular public, falsifiable model. Live burden: He must specify what adequate disclosure would involve, justify the expectation from God’s capacities, and demonstrate that disputed experiences and arguments genuinely fail that standard. Locked score: A 78 appropriately rewards the intelligible inference and exceptionally direct debate contact while withholding credit because the pivotal absence claim is asserted broadly, with limited precision and charitable engagement.
